_README: LITERAL golden vectors for the Model B contractual payment schedule.
WHY LITERALS, AND NOT GENERATED VALUES
The schedule generator is implemented three times: disclosure-service,
origination-service and servicing-service each carry their own
app/schedule.py. They cannot import a shared module -- separate images,
no shared internal package (ADR 0004 records how the copies arose).
db/tools/golden_schedule_vectors.py can print these numbers, and a test
that compares a service against that script proves only that two pieces
of code agree. If the shared understanding of Model B is wrong, they
agree on the wrong answer and every suite stays green. The values below
are checked in as data and were verified independently, so a change to
any implementation -- including the reference one -- has to disagree with
a number a human signed off on.
HOW THESE WERE VERIFIED
Each value was recomputed at 60 significant digits and cross-checked by
hand:
* the exact unrounded level payment, before rounding, so that a value
sitting near a half-cent boundary is known to round the way it does.
BOARDING-24 is exactly that case: the exact payment is
407.004576918..., which is 407.00 -- a generator that rounded up
would produce 407.01 and be wrong by a cent on every one of 23
periods.
* first-period interest as principal x rate / 12, at full precision,
* regular_payment x regular_payment_count + final_payment ==
total_of_payments, checked by hand for all five vectors.
* finance_charge == total_of_payments - amount_financed, likewise.
WHAT MODEL B IS
Regular periods bill the cent-rounded level payment. The FINAL period
bills remaining principal plus that period's interest, so the payment
absorbs the accumulated cent residue instead of the principal column
hiding it. Therefore:
* total_of_payments is the SUM OF ACTUAL PAYMENTS, not the unrounded
payment multiplied by the term;
* finance_charge = total_of_payments - amount_financed;
* the APR is solved from the actual payment SEQUENCE including the
adjusted final payment -- a level-payment solve prices a cash flow
nobody receives.
amount_financed is principal less the 3.0% prepaid origination fee.
SCOPE OF THE APR FIGURES
The `apr` values are this system's own actuarial solve, carried here so
a change to the solver is caught. They are NOT independently certified:
no outside oracle has confirmed them. The FFIEC APR Computational Tool
check remains outstanding and is tracked as the one blocker on PR #10
that code cannot close. Do not cite these as FFIEC-verified.
ADDING A VECTOR
Verify it the way described above before adding it. Regenerating it from
the reference script and pasting the output defeats the purpose of the
file -- at that point the literals are just a cache of the code.

LIVE-48._why: The live example that exposed the original defect: the application disclosed an APR derived from an add-on ratio. 48 months is also the longest term in use, so it accumulates the most rounding residue.

RV-2-36._why: The second real application vector reproduced against the defect (15,000 / 7.99% / 36). Its final payment is LOWER than the regular one, unlike LIVE-48 -- so an implementation that assumed the final adjustment always rounds upward fails here and nowhere else.

ZERO-RATE-36._why: Promotional 0%. The amortization formula divides by zero at a zero monthly rate, so this vector is the only one that proves the principal/term branch exists. Note the APR is 1.987 and NOT zero: the prepaid fee alone makes borrowing cost something, which is exactly the distinction between a note rate and an APR.

SHORT-HIGH-6._why: Short term, high rate. Six periods leave almost no room to absorb residue, and a 35.9% APR is far enough from the 24.99% note rate that a copy which confuses the two cannot pass by coincidence.

BOARDING-24._why: The rounding-boundary case, and the vector the boarding tests use. The exact level payment is 407.004576918..., a hair above 407.00 -- so it pins the rounding direction on a value where getting it wrong costs a cent on each of 23 periods. Its disclosed APR (11.029) is also well clear of its note rate (7.99), which is what makes the boarding tests able to prove the right one was written to loans.apr.
